input_template: Configure a simpeg prediction case for tem_decay: Time-domain electromagnetic (TEM) central-loop decay measurement; normalized dB/dt vs. time after transmitter turn-off. Outputs: apparent resistivity (Ω·m), impedance phase (°), transient EMF (normalized), or apparent chargeability (dimensionless) as a function of electrode spacing / frequency / time. Use the following parameterization: sigma_bg = {value_0} S/m for background electrical conductivity of the host rock; electrical conductivity of the anomaly body (sigma_anomaly) takes {value_1} S/m; depth_top (top depth of the anomaly body) is {value_2} m; depth_bottom, representing bottom depth of the anomaly body, is set to {value_3} m; width_x = {value_4} m for horizontal width of the anomaly body. Additional controls are vertical thickness of the anomaly body (width_z) takes {value_5} m; source_spacing (transmitter-receiver electrode spacing (DC/IP) or loop radius (TEM)) is {value_6} m; noise_level, representing relative measurement noise level (fraction of signal), is set to {value_7}; n_layers = {value_8} for number of horizontal earth layers in the model; total survey profile length (survey_length) takes {value_9} m. Remaining physical or categorical settings are chargeability (intrinsic chargeability (Cole-Cole model, IP/TEM scenarios)) is {value_10}; time_constant, representing Cole-Cole relaxation time constant (IP) or TEM decay time constant, is set to {value_11} s; freq_min = {value_12} Hz for minimum MT sounding frequency; maximum MT sounding frequency (freq_max) takes {value_13} Hz; mu_r (relative magnetic permeability) is {value_14}. Use full survey curve, 100 measurement points; observed channels: measurement channel 1 (1 of 1) and predict geophysical_response.
target_template: Model output for geophysical_response:{output_0}

input_template: Configure a simpeg prediction case for tem_decay: Time-domain electromagnetic (TEM) central-loop decay measurement; normalized dB/dt vs. time after transmitter turn-off. The governing context is Geophysical inversion simulation (SimPEG). Elliptic PDE: ∇·(σ∇φ) = −Iδ. 1D layered earth model solved analytically (DC/IP) or via transfer-matrix method (MT/TEM). Outputs: apparent resistivity (Ω·m), impedance phase (°), transient EMF (normalized), or apparent chargeability (dimensionless) as a function of electrode spacing / frequency / time. Use the following parameterization: sigma_bg = {value_0} S/m for background electrical conductivity of the host rock; electrical conductivity of the anomaly body (sigma_anomaly) takes {value_1} S/m; depth_top (top depth of the anomaly body) is {value_2} m; depth_bottom, representing bottom depth of the anomaly body, is set to {value_3} m; width_x = {value_4} m for horizontal width of the anomaly body. Additional controls are vertical thickness of the anomaly body (width_z) takes {value_5} m; source_spacing (transmitter-receiver electrode spacing (DC/IP) or loop radius (TEM)) is {value_6} m; noise_level, representing relative measurement noise level (fraction of signal), is set to {value_7}; n_layers = {value_8} for number of horizontal earth layers in the model; total survey profile length (survey_length) takes {value_9} m. Remaining physical or categorical settings are chargeability (intrinsic chargeability (Cole-Cole model, IP/TEM scenarios)) is {value_10}; time_constant, representing Cole-Cole relaxation time constant (IP) or TEM decay time constant, is set to {value_11} s; freq_min = {value_12} Hz for minimum MT sounding frequency; maximum MT sounding frequency (freq_max) takes {value_13} Hz; mu_r (relative magnetic permeability) is {value_14}. Use full survey curve, 100 measurement points; observed channels: measurement channel 1 (1 of 1) and predict geophysical_response.
target_template: Model output for geophysical_response:{output_0}
